old: It honors a 19th-century British officer, not a fabric or shape.
The garment's name is literally someone's title — an earl's.
That earl was James Brudenell, 7th Earl of a Welsh town's name.
clues: This piece of knitwear is named after a man, not a pattern or a place: a British earl who served as a military commander in the 1800s.
It is a knitted top that opens all the way down the front and usually fastens with buttons, unlike a pullover sweater you tug on over your head.
You might throw one over a blouse on a chilly office day, and Mister Rogers famously changed into one at the start of every episode.
